The decree having attained finality, the respondent initiated execution proceedings before the trial Court/executing Court' During pendency of the execution petition, the petitioner/judgmentdebtor moved an application seeking permission to discharge the decretal liability by payment of Rs.5,000/- per month as pleading financial hardship.

7. I have heard the leamed counsel for the parties and have carefully gone through the available record.

E. It is settled law that dower (Haq Mehr) is an obligatory debt upon the husband and its prompt payment is enforceable through legal process. At the same time, it is equally well-established that execution proceedings are meant to enforce a decree and not to punish thejudgment-debtor.

9. The discretion to allorv payment of decretal amount in installments isjudicial in nature, to be exercised fairly, reasonably and equitably, keeping in view the financial capaclty of the judgmentdebtor, thenature of the decretal amount, and the likelihood of actual satisfaction of the decree within a reasonable time.

10. In the present case, it is not disputed that the govemment servant seryrng as a lsa police official, having a fixed and limited income but the record reflects that he is burdened with multiple dependents, including aged parents. These factors were not properly appreciated by the Courts below. As the Executing Court was justified in observing that the proposed payment of Rs.5,000/per month was insufficient, the outright dismissal of the application, without fixing a reasonable installment after balancing the rights of the decreeholder with the paying capaclty of the judgmentdebtor, amounts to a failure to properly exercise discretion in accordance with law. The purpose of allowing installments is to ensure real and effective execution of the decree. An order which makes compliance practically impossible would neither serve the ends of justice nor advance the cause of equity.
11. In family matters, Courts are expected adopt a compassionate and pragmatic approach, that enforcement of rigfuts does not result in undue hardship or social dislocation.

12. Keeping in view the financial status of the petitioner, his service profile, and the legitimate right of the respondent to recover her dower within a reasonable timeframe, this Court is of the considered view tltat fixation of Rs.25,000/- per month as installment strikes a fair balance between competing equities.

13. For the foregoing reasons, this writ petition to so is allowed. Consequently, the impugned orders passed by the learned Executing Court and the leamed Additional District Judge-II, Bannu, are hereby set aside. The petitioner is directed to satisfi the decretal dower amount by palng monthly of Rs.25,000/-, per month. The petitioner is further directed to clear the arrears of dower accrued for the period from 0l-09-2023 to 3l-12-2025, by making payment at the same rate of Rs.25,000/- per month, in lumpsum or in such manner as may be calculated accordingly and thereafter continued monthly payment till the satisfaction of decree. In case of two consecutive defaults, the respondent shall be at liberty to seek enforcement ofthe decree through coercive process in accordance with law.
